```{r}
# Assuming your pre-computed hclust object is named: cbb_hclust
# CRITICAL: The labels inside your 'cbb_hclust' object MUST match 
# the column names of your matrix and the row names of your annotation.

# 1. Update your unique keys vector to match whatever labels are inside your hclust object
# Run: labels(cbb_hclust) in your console to see what they look like!
unique_keys <- labels(cbb) 

# 2. Assign those exact labels to your matrix and annotation dataframe
colnames(heatmap_matrix_scaled) <- unique_keys
rownames(annotation_col)        <- unique_keys

# 3. Pass your actual hclust object directly into the heatmap
pheatmap(
  heatmap_matrix_scaled,
  annotation_col = annotation_col,
  show_colnames = FALSE,         
  cluster_rows = TRUE,           # Let pheatmap cluster the traits (rows)
  cluster_cols = cbb_hclust,     # <--- FORCES pheatmap to use YOUR sample dendrogram!
  main = "Physiological Profiles Ordered by Custom CBB Dendrogram"
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(pheatmap)

# 1. Join your datasets and strip duplicates immediately to get a clean baseline
combined_df_unique <- cluster_summary %>%
  inner_join(df_clean_numeric, by = "SampleID_clean") %>%
  distinct(SampleID_clean, .keep_all = TRUE)

# 2. Extract your traits matrix
my_physiological_traits <- c("Quant", "Sigma", "Connect", "Tau1", "Tau2", "qm", "nTau2", "nTau1", "nCon", "Fo", "Fm")

heatmap_matrix <- combined_df_unique %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(my_physiological_traits)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  dplyr::select(where(~ var(., na.rm = TRUE) > 0)) %>% 
  as.matrix()

# 3. Transpose and scale
heatmap_matrix_scaled <- t(scale(heatmap_matrix))

# 4. Create an explicit, unique naming vector to bind the matrix and annotations
# We will use row indexes concatenated with the ID to ensure 100% unique tracking
unique_keys <- paste0("ID_", 1:ncol(heatmap_matrix_scaled), "_", combined_df_unique$SampleID_clean)

# Assign these keys to the matrix columns
colnames(heatmap_matrix_scaled) <- unique_keys


# 5. Build your annotation dataframe using the EXACT same unique keys as rownames
annotation_col <- combined_df_unique %>% 
  dplyr::select(species.x, K_3.x) %>% # Double-check your exact K column names here!
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Force the row names to match the matrix column names exactly
rownames(annotation_col) <- unique_keys


# 6. Plot the heatmap
pheatmap(
  heatmap_matrix_scaled,
  annotation_col = annotation_col,
  show_colnames = FALSE,         
  cluster_rows = TRUE,           
  cluster_cols = TRUE,           
  clustering_method = "ward.D2", 
  main = "Physiological Profiles vs. K-Cluster Assignments"
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(pheatmap)

# 1. Join your datasets
combined_df <- cluster_summary %>%
  inner_join(df_clean_numeric, by = "SampleID_clean")

# 2. CRITICAL STEP: Keep only the FIRST unique occurrence of each Sample ID
# This prevents the duplicate row.names error entirely!
combined_df_unique <- combined_df %>%
  distinct(SampleID_clean, .keep_all = TRUE)


# 3. Define your traits and build the matrix using the unique dataframe
my_physiological_traits <- c("Quant", "Sigma", "Connect", "Tau1", "Tau2", "qm", "nTau2", "nTau1", "nCon", "Fo", "Fm")

# --- 3. Build the matrix and clean up missing/zero-variance data ---
heatmap_matrix <- combined_df_unique %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(my_physiological_traits)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  # Fix 1: Dynamically remove traits that have absolutely zero variance
  dplyr::select(where(~ var(., na.rm = TRUE) > 0)) %>% 
  as.matrix()

# --- 4. Scale, transpose, and handle residual NAs ---
# Transpose and scale
heatmap_matrix_scaled <- t(scale(heatmap_matrix))

annotation_col <- combined_df_unique %>% 
  dplyr::select(species.x, K_4.x) %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Fix 2: If any NAs are still lingering, replace them with 0 
# (Since the data is z-score scaled, 0 perfectly represents the "trait average")
# heatmap_matrix_scaled[is.na(heatmap_matrix_scaled)] <- 0
# heatmap_matrix_scaled[is.infinite(heatmap_matrix_scaled)] <- 0

# Assign your unique sample names safely
colnames(heatmap_matrix_scaled) <- combined_df_unique$SampleID_clean



# This will now work perfectly because all names are guaranteed unique
rownames(annotation_col) <- colnames(heatmap_matrix_scaled)


# 5. Plot the heatmap
pheatmap(
  heatmap_matrix_scaled,
  annotation_col = annotation_col,
  show_colnames = FALSE,         
  cluster_rows = TRUE,           
  cluster_cols = TRUE,           
  clustering_method = "ward.D2", 
  main = "Physiological Profiles vs. K-Cluster Assignments"
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# --- STEP 1: Define your actual physiological traits ---
# Replace these placeholder names with the actual column names of your biological data!

  dplyr::select(all_of(my_physiological_traits)) %>%

  as.matrix()

colnames(heatmap_matrix_scaled) <- cluster_summary$SampleID_clean

  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# --- STEP 3: Run the heatmap ---
pheatmap(
  heatmap_matrix_scaled,
  annotation_col = annotation_col,

  cluster_cols = TRUE,           # This will group samples by their physiological profiles
  clustering_method = "ward.D2", 
  main = "Physiological Profiles vs. K-Cluster Assignments"
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(pheatmap)

# --- STEP 1: Separate your continuous numeric data from your metadata ---
# Make sure you ONLY include true numeric physiological traits here (e.g., physiological data columns)
# Do NOT include species or sample IDs in this matrix!
trait_columns <- c( "K_2", "K_3", "K_4", "K_5") # Double-check these are strictly numeric data columns

heatmap_matrix <- cluster_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(trait_columns)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>% # Forces everything to be numeric
  as.matrix()

# Transpose and scale (z-score) so traits are rows and samples are columns
heatmap_matrix_scaled <- t(scale(heatmap_matrix))

# Assign clear sample names to the matrix columns
colnames(heatmap_matrix_scaled) <- cluster_summary$SampleID_clean


# --- STEP 2: Create a true data.frame (not a tibble) for annotations ---
annotation_col <- cluster_summary %>% 
  dplyr::select(species, K_3) %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor)) %>%
  as.data.frame() # <--- CRITICAL: Converts tibble to data.frame so row names work

# Safely set the row names now that it is a standard data.frame
rownames(annotation_col) <- colnames(heatmap_matrix_scaled)


# --- STEP 3: Run pheatmap ---
pheatmap(
  heatmap_matrix_scaled,
  annotation_col = annotation_col,
  show_colnames = FALSE,         
  cluster_rows = TRUE,           
  cluster_cols = TRUE,           
  clustering_method = "ward.D2", 
  main = "Physiological Heatmap"
)
```
